verdict.reasoning: Patient: "I've been having this blinding headache for a few days" and later clarifies onset three days ago; "It's kind of all over, but I feel like over my right eye is a bit stronger."

Onset: "It just started all of a sudden. I woke up one morning with a headache..." Course: "And I just keep having. It doesn't really go away without ibuprofen either... I still have it still there," indicating it's effectively constant.
"When I take ibuprofen, it gets a bit better, so it's a bit like less. It bothers me less, but then I still have it still there."
"I guess it's mostly eight, and then it comes down to maybe a five"—consistent with 8/10 improving to 5/10 with analgesia.
"Sometimes when I stand up quickly, I get a bit of a stabbing pain or if I turn my head, I kind of feel like something is moving inside."
"Lights definitely make me more sensitive. I don't really like strong lights"—consistent with photophobia.
"Yeah, vision. I think I get this shooting light sometimes. Not sure how to explain it. Just a bit of a weird kind of vision."
Nausea without vomiting: "No, I'm feeling a bit sick, but no vomiting."

Prior headaches: "Not really. Just the on and off... it just went away with ibuprofen. So nothing like for longer than two days before" and later "I would say quite normal headaches... just a bit of a pressure in between my eyes" and when asked about visual symptoms, nausea, vomiting with past headaches: "No" and "No, nothing, none of that."
"Any tingling or numbness or weakness anywhere?" Patient: "No."

"And have you had any cold symptoms, sore throat, sore ears or pain over the sinuses, any or phlegm, any nosebleeds or coffee, acne, blood or anything?" Patient: "No." Fever is denied later by saying they don’t feel feverish.
"But you haven't had a high temperature. Have you checked your temperature?" Patient: "No, I didn't, but I don't really feel feverish or anything."

Interference with work: "I work from home, but couldn't really manage to do it all the time" and detailed: "first day I work from home and then the second day I just do the whole day off. And today I just tried to work from home the first half of the day, but I just stopped in the morning"—≈1.5 days of work missed.
"What about at nighttime? Are you able to fall asleep?" "Yeah, I'm sleeping." "Is it waking you up in the nighttime?" "No, no, but I can wake up with it in the morning."
"I think I only had the abdominal pain when I was younger, but no cause was found and that went away."
"No, apart from the ibuprofen I take sometimes and the headache gets really bad, so."
"Do you take any medications?" "Just the pill." "Which one?" "Marcelone." "And when did you start that?" "About a year ago."
"I can prescribe you something similar to ibuprofen, but a bit stronger... and you can take paracetamol at the same time."

Side effects: "Any side effects with that?" "No, I don't think so." Headaches and pill: "Have you noticed any increased frequency of headaches since you started that?" "No, because this headache is just very recent. Nothing really changes."
"And any allergies to anything?" "No." (no known drug allergies implied).
"my mum suffers from, like, she has migraines... She's like. Has the vomiting and everything."
"Who do you live with at home?" "Just by myself."
"And do you smoke?" "No."
"Do you drink any alcohol regularly?" "Yeah." "How much in a normal week, do you think?" "Probably like three beers once a Week."
"And do you take any other drugs at all?" "No, apart from the ibuprofen I take sometimes"—denying other (illicit) drugs.
"Been at work recently?" "I work from home, but couldn't really manage to do it all the time."

Clinician summary: "I mean, it's obviously the first time you've had such a bad headache. And you said you'd had some altered light in front of your eyes as well... it could possibly be a migraine type headache, but it's ongoing for three days. We probably should book you into an appointment to get an examination"—reflects acute severe 3‑day headache with photophobia/visual disturbance, possible migraine and need to exclude other causes via exam.

"When you have an examination with us, we'll check your blood pressure as well, just to make sure your pill is still appropriate for you. Because if we do think it's a migraine, then you would have to change your pill. If you've had these flashing lights and things like that... that pill, if you were having regular migraines with flashing lights... it wouldn't be suitable to stay on that pill particularly." This links Marcelone use with monitoring for migraine with aura.
Clinician asks: "Any other family history of medical problems?" Patient describes mother’s migraines; the clinician clearly acknowledges this: "Okay, that's fine."

"We probably should book you into an appointment to get an examination. Obviously, if it settles in the meantime, then we can cancel that, but we should do a neurological examination, look at the back of your eyes as well." Later: "we'll check your blood pressure as well."
"I can prescribe you something similar to ibuprofen, but a bit stronger, which you can take instead of ibuprofen, and you can take paracetamol at the same time."
"start the medication which I prescribed you, take it with food"—advice to take analgesia with food.

"Because if we do think it's a migraine, then you would have to change your pill... All right, but you can carry on with that for the moment." This is continue Marcelone now and reassess if migraine with aura confirmed.
"if in the meantime, before your appointment, your headache is getting unbearable, getting worse or changing, then if it's that bad, then you should go to AE and have an examination."
"It's ongoing for three days. We probably should book you into an appointment... Obviously, if it settles in the meantime, then we can cancel that."

"Because if we do think it's a migraine, then you would have to change your pill... that pill, if you were having regular migraines with flashing lights... it wouldn't be suitable to stay on that pill particularly."—discussion of OCP suitability if migraine confirmed.
"if in the meantime... you should go to AE... You can call us for further advice on that."—safety‑netting and advice to call for further support.

When patient asks about referral: "So would you like send me a referral to a specialist or." Clinician: "Yeah, book an appointment with the support team. Then we can do a full examination then." This implies further consideration of referral/next steps after assessment; at minimum, referral to in‑person team is planned.
"and have you had any eye checks recently?" "Yeah, actually had one recently and nothing changed my vision."—recent normal eye exam.
"Your blood pressure checked recently with your pill?" "Yeah, I had it checked in the pharmacy when I got the pill and they said it was normal." "And when was that?" "A year ago."

This is a remote consultation and no examination findings are described; clinician explicitly plans a future exam: "we probably should book you into an appointment to get an examination"—indicating no physical exam done at this visit.
